chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about a man who performed li'an (cursing) with his wife, so he swore four testimonies by Allah, then abstained (from swearing) in the fifth. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he abstained in the fifth, then she is his wife, and he is whipped; and if the woman abstained from that, when the oath is upon her, then upon her is similar to that.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'And I asked him about the cursing, would he curse standing or sitting?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The cursing and what resembles it is from standing.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And I asked him about a man who divorced his wife before he entered (consummated) with her, so she claimed that she was pregnant. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she establishes the proof that he loosened the veil (consummated), then denies the child, he can curse her, then she is irrevocably divorced from him, and upon him is the complete dower.'

key_terms.سِتْرًا: Veil or covering (referring to the marital bed/consummation)
key_terms.لَاعَنَ: Performed li'an (mutual cursing/oath-taking to resolve paternity dispute)
key_terms.نَكَلَ: Abstained or hesitated from swearing the oath

ai.seo_question: What are the legal consequences of li'an if the husband or wife abstains from the fifth oath, and how is dower handled in pre-consummation divorce with pregnancy claims?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the procedural mechanics of li'an, emphasizing that the physical posture (standing or sitting) is secondary to the verbal declaration, a nuance highlighted by Imam al-Sadiq (AS). It further clarifies the specific application of li'an in cases of pre-consummation divorce where paternity is disputed, linking the dissolution of marriage to the payment of the full dower. These rulings underscore the Shia jurisprudential focus on the precise conditions of the fifth oath and the evidentiary burden in establishing lineage.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who cursed his wife, so he swore on oath by Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with four testimonies, then abstained regarding the fifth. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he abstained regarding the fifth, so she is his wife, and he would be whipped, and if the woman abstained from that, when there was a swear against her, so upon her is similar to that’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the cursing, would he curse standing or sitting?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The cursing and what resembles it is from standing’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who divorces his wife before he copulates with her, so she claims that she is pregnant. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If she establishes the proof that he loosened the veil then denies the child, he can curse her and she would be irrevocably divorced from him, and upon him is the complete dower’.
en.sarwar: 12. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-‘Amrakiy ibn Ali from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who has said the following:

“I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who goes through the process of al-Li ‘an (condemnation) against his woman and testifies swearing by Allah four times but declines the fifth time. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he declines the fifth time she is his woman but he is whipped. If the woman declines when swearing is on her, she is subjected to the same process as he was.’
I then asked if al-Li‘an (condemnation) is completed in a sitting or standing position. He (the Imam) said, ‘Al-Li‘an (condemnation) and similar things are done in a standing position.’

“I then asked about a man who has divorced his wife before going to bed with her and then claims that she is pregnant. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he presents proof that he has uncovered a secret then denies the child to be his child, he can go through the process of al-Li‘an (condemnation) and she becomes stranger to him, but he must pay the mahr (dower).’”
